evidence.claim: The Centennial Scenic Byway forms a 163-mile horseshoe between Dubois and Pinedale, crossing badlands, ranch land and high mountain country.
evidence.quote: The 163 miles between Pinedale and Dubois comprise the Wyoming Centennial Scenic Byway. This horseshoe-shaped combination of highways includes U.S. 26/287 and U.S. 26/89/191. The route crosses diverse landscapes including badlands, ranch land, and the high montane.

flags: Pass elevation differs: DOT and tourism say 9,658 feet; cache 28 says 9,655. Elevation omitted. Forest Service intro says 162 miles but later says 163; 163 agrees with DOT and tourism.
Road construction and campaigning are not documented; the overview uses the supported 1989 designation and earlier travel history.
DOT brochure is dated 2000 and has unrelated factual errors (Yellowstone designation year and river drainage). Practical note records cache review only, not live road status.
Rendezvous landmark status does not establish public access to the ranch road. No invitation to enter private land or precise access directions included.
Togwotee’s tribal affiliation is not repeated without a community source; cache 28 uses Sheepeater tribe and Shoshones, while other cache pages use Mountain Shoshone.
